business_scope.primary_industry_name: Multi-Channel Omni-Helpdesk and Conversational Bot Cloud

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt — National One-Stop Incorporation Window at the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Constitutional Islamic Sharia as principal source of legislation per Constitution Article 2; Egyptian Civil Code No. 131 of 1948)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: COMESA (Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa)
Double Taxation Agreements with UAE, Germany, UK, France, China, India, Kuwait and 45+ other states (no US-Egypt income tax treaty)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2023; UBO register obligations under the Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (Articles 487-500 for LLC) as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 (GAFI registration); Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; Counter-Terrorism Law No. 94 of 2015; Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) KYC directives; supervision by the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and legalized Power of Attorney appointing the local incorporation representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-state Notary Public or Egyptian Consulate in the signatory's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Egypt acceded; verify current HCCH status table) OR Egyptian Consular Legalization where apostille is unavailable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ultimate Beneficial Owner declaration (GAFI/EMLCU prescribed UBO Form) with shareholding and control chart
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All natural-person shareholders/UBOs, authenticated before the Ministry of Justice Notary Public (Misr al-Tawtheeq)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: In-country notarization with GAFI e-submission; foreign UBO signature pages consular/apostille legalized as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports and proof of residential address for UBOs and the resident manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or Consular Legalization, plus certified Arabic translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and board resolution of the corporate shareholder (if any) authorizing establishment of the Egyptian LLC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-state Companies Registry / Chamber of Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or Consular Legalization, plus certified Arabic translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / compliance clearance for incorporation capital (no statutory minimum capital required)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Egyptian bank issuing the initial deposit certificate under CBE KYC framework
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank-stamped document filed at the GAFI One-Stop-Shop

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, shareholders, managers, and counterparties against: (i) OFAC SDN List; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List (1267/1988); (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) Egyptian domestic terrorism list under Counter-Terrorism Law No. 94 of 2015 via EMLCU; and (v) sanctions notices of the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. PEP verification is mandatory for foreign and domestic politically exposed persons (heads of state, senior executive, judicial, legislative, and military officials, plus family members and close associates) per Law No. 80 of 2002 and CBE KYC Rules. Enhanced Due Diligence applies to high-risk jurisdictions; CDD records must be retained for five years following termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Online Services Portal ('Invest in Egypt') name reservation module, verified against the unified Commercial Registry database of the Ministry of Trade and Industry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A statutory Arabic company name is mandatory for all LLCs; the Arabic name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name or to well-known marks. A transliterated English trade name may be registered as a secondary style provided it does not violate prior trademark rights. All foreign-language attachments require certified Arabic translation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Financial, Insurance, Takaful (require Financial Regulatory Authority approval)
Central, National, Government, Ministry, President, Presidency, State (require ministerial clearance)
Egypt, Egyptian, Arab Republic (require express GAFI / Ministry of Trade authorization)
Military, Armed Forces, Police, Intelligence (prohibited for private LLCs)
Islamic, Jihad, Terrorist, or any religious or political denomination capable of misleading the public (prohibited by public-order clause)
Petroleum, Gas, Mining, Aviation, Telecom, Nuclear, Space (subject to sectoral licensing prerequisites)
Holding, International, Group, Development (admissible only upon substantiation of business scope and capital substance)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The approved name reservation is renewable once for an additional 60 days upon payment of the renewal service fee. Upon formal rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative objection with the GAFI Commercial Registry Division within 15 calendar days of the rejection notice, attaching alternative name choices and trademark search evidence; if the objection is refused, the applicant may escalate to the competent administrative court under the State Council (Conseil d'État). Name-search fees are non-refundable per attempt.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted with conditions: GAFI and the Commercial Registry accept a registered address in Egypt, including licensed virtual-office and flex-space addresses in Cairo, Giza, Alexandria, or the New Administrative Capital, for a digital-services LLC; the LLC must, however, maintain books and records at the address and accept legal service of process there. Banking counterparties and payment integrators (Stripe/PayPal via an Egyptian bank account) generally require a physically attended or clearly staffed commercial address; a purely virtual presence heightens KYB scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 10-15% estimated probability of an unannounced physical verification by GAFI or the Commercial Registry within the first 36 months for an IT/helpdesk entity rated Low_Risk_Standard; probability rises to 40-60% upon AML/TF flags, inconsistent UBO declarations, or a virtual office without verifiable human presence.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GAFI company name reservation and clearance fee (electronic search)
GAFI One-Stop-Shop incorporation document filing fee for LLC (no statutory minimum capital)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 fee schedule; prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Ministry of Justice Notary Public (Misr al-Tawtheeq) authentication of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarization statutory tariff scaled to declared share capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Registry certificate issuance (data bank registration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry — Commercial Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976 tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax registration and tax card issuance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tax-card issuance fee under Law No. 91 of 2005

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation announcement in the Official Gazette / two daily newspapers
Certified Arabic translation of foreign UBO, passport, and power-of-attorney documents (estimated 25 pages at USD 6 per page)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice accredited translation bureau

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization of foreign-issued corporate documents (5 documents at approximately USD 80 each)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home-state Competent Apostille Authority / Egyptian Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedule or home-state apostille tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / virtual office address for the first statutory year (Cairo flex-space)
Local incorporation attorney fee (corporate secretarial and UBO compliance pack)
Contingency reserve for additional endorsements, fiscal stamps, and administrative amendments

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended), together with the Executive Regulations issued by Prime Minister's Decree No. 96 of 1982; limited liability companies are further subject to the Commercial Registration Law and the unified VAT and tax registration rules administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - One-Stop Shop / Integrated Services Office, acting with the Commercial Registry of the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Contract (Eaqd al-Tasis) and annexed Articles of Association, submitted through the GAFI company registration electronic portal, with registration effected in the Commercial Register (Qayd al-Sharikat).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on an LLC under the Investment Law; the capital must be divided into quotas, fully subscribed at incorporation and paid up within the statutory period not exceeding five years; a bank certificate confirming the capital deposit or escrow account in Egypt is required by GAFI before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The founders, having subscribed to the Company's entire share capital, shall cause such capital to be deposited in the designated bank account opened in the name of the LLC under formation; (2) The Company adopts its registered office and legal address at the premises located in Cairo, Egypt, as specified in the incorporation contract, and the General Manager is authorized to execute the lease agreement and register the address with the competent authorities; (3) The General Manager, Financial Manager, and Company Secretary are appointed, and the General Manager is authorized to execute all formation documents and complete filings before the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones, the Egyptian Tax Authority, the Commercial Registry, and any other governmental offices.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI - Invest in Egypt online portal and the Commercial Registry name index
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the GAFI electronic services portal, complete the Company Name Reservation application for the LLC, select one Arabic name and one transliterated English name, pay the reservation fee online, and obtain the electronic name reservation certificate which is valid for a limited statutory period; the name must not conflict with registered trademarks, existing corporate names, or prohibited religious/public-order terms.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copy of each founder
Signed name reservation application form
Notarized power of attorney if an agent submits the application
Proposed business purpose description (ISIC 6201 helpdesk services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or public-order grounds, the applicant may submit a written re-consideration request to the GAFI naming committee within 15 days, or amend and resubmit a new name reservation application without additional penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Incorporation Contract and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice Notary Public Office and a licensed Egyptian bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the incorporation contract in the Arabic language, setting out the LLC's corporate purpose, quota capital allocation, registered office address, management structure, profit-sharing rules and duration; all founders or their authorized attorneys must sign the contract in the presence of the notary public; simultaneously open a temporary bank account titled 'Company under Formation' and obtain a capital deposit certificate evidencing the paid-up quotas.
required_dossiers: Valid passport/national ID of each founder
Company name reservation certificate
Certified Arabic draft of the incorporation contract
Lease agreement or title deed for the intended registered office
Power of attorney duly notarized and legalized for foreign founders
Bank capital deposit certificate or escrow account confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses execution because a foreign signature lacks apostille or consular legalization, obtain the required legalization through the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant consulate, then re-present the authenticated documents; any notarial query on the corporate purpose shall be cured by amending the purpose clause to the exact IT-services description.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Commercial Registration and Issuance of the Corporate Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / Integrated Services Office and Commercial Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation dossier to the GAFI one-stop shop, either electronically or in person; GAFI reviews legal compliance, validates the paid-up capital certificate and the notarized incorporation contract, collects the prescribed registration fees, and instructs the Commercial Registry to issue the Certificate of Company Registration containing the Commercial Registration (CR) number; this certificate is the LLC's legal personality evidence.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation contract and articles of association
Capital deposit certificate from the Egyptian bank
Company name reservation certificate
Lease agreement of the registered office
Passport copies and powers of attorney of all founders
Completed GAFI registration application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a deficiency query, the applicant has 10 working days to cure the missing items without additional filing fees; where the query relates to an unsubstantiated capital deposit, present an updated bank statement or re-open the escrow account; on expiry of the cure period, a new submission may be required under GAFI's re-filing procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Egyptian Tax Authority Registration and Unified Tax Card
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Taxpayer Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Commercial Registration certificate and the incorporation contract to the ETA to obtain the Unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) and the Unified Tax Card; register for corporate income tax, payroll and withholding tax, stamp tax, and VAT where annual taxable turnover exceeds the statutory threshold; the tax card must list the Cairo registered office address and the helpdesk SaaS commercial activity.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate
Notarized incorporation contract
Valid lease agreement of the registered premises
Power of attorney and passport copies of the legal representative
Bank account details and capital deposit certificate
Completed ETA tax registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA delays issuance pending a physical inspection of the premises, arrange an inspection appointment and submit the lease contract and utility bill proving actual occupation; inconsistencies in the stated purpose shall be rectified by filing an amended incorporation extract and a written explanation to the ETA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Official Gazette Publication and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Gazette (Al-Waqai Al-Masriyyah) and the National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the statutory incorporation abstract in the Official Gazette, as this extract may be required for banking and notarial matters; register the LLC as an employer with the competent NOSI office in the company's district, submit the constitutional contract and the projected payroll data, and open a social insurance file for the General Manager and any employees.
required_dossiers: GAFI Commercial Registration certificate
Notarized incorporation contract and extract
Official Gazette publication fee receipt
Passports and national IDs of managers and employees
Lease agreement of the registered office
Completed NOSI employer registration Form 1
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Official Gazette requests correction of an incorporation abstract error, submit a formal correction request accompanied by the original certificate and court-filing permission if required; NOSI queries on wage estimates shall be resolved by submitting salary statements and a revised payroll declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Chamber of Commerce Registration and Business Premises License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce and the local district administrative authority (Hayy/Unit of Local Administration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LLC in the commercial register at the competent Chamber of Commerce to obtain the membership certificate required for import/export and official formalities; apply to the local district administration for the business premises operation license (Rukhsat al-Mahall), providing the civil defense fire-safety approval, building lease, and a layout plan of the helpdesk office.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate
Chamber of Commerce membership application
Civil defense fire-safety approval for the premises
Approved building layout plan
Lease agreement and land/building tax receipt
Passport and power of attorney of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the district administration refuses or delays the premises license due to zoning or building-code findings, submit an appeal with supporting documentation to the Governor's Licensing Committee; where fire-safety clearance is outstanding, remedy the cited defects and obtain a fresh Civil Defense inspection report.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the Helpdesk SaaS activity is classified as a non-industrial Information Technology and IT-Enabled Service; no manufacturing or industrial operating license from the Industrial Development Authority (IDA) is required; the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) supervises the ICT sector generally.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required as a statutory industrial permit; however, if the LLC processes the personal data of end users or client firms, the company should consider filing the voluntary/required Data Controller Registration with the Data Protection Authority under the Personal Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020; a consumer assistance helpline serving Egyptian consumers may also require a service-practice notification to the Consumer Protection Agency.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) acting under Law No. 4 of 1994 as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 'C' - Exempt / Simplified Registration for low-impact office-based IT services and helpdesk operations; a full Environmental Impact Assessment is not required because the activity involves no manufacturing, combustion, or chemical discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions are anticipated; the facility must comply with EEAA general office environmental requirements including separate collection and licensed disposal of e-waste, electrical battery and UPS recycling rules, indoor noise levels not exceeding 45 dB(A) in open workspace, and proper ventilation at server/telephony equipment rooms.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The LLC must obtain a fire safety inspection certificate from the General Administration for Civil Defense of the Ministry of Interior confirming working fire extinguishers, emergency exit signage, smoke detectors and evacuation arrangements; a structural/occupational clearance of the leased floor shall be issued by a licensed engineering office verifying floor loading for IT equipment; the Ministry of Manpower provides an occupational health and safety clearance under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 covering workstations, ergonomics, first aid kits, and electrical safety for the helpdesk staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance — unified TIN/tax card registry and VAT administration; official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing/e-receipt platform: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg. Company incorporation and tax registration are co-administered with GAFI (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones) through the one-stop shop.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Form EG_LLC with GAFI (100% foreign ownership allowed, no minimum capital) and complete Commercial Registry filing. Step 2: File the ETA establishment declaration and issue a power of attorney to a local accredited tax representative within 90 days of commercial registration to obtain the unified tax card (TIN). Step 3: Register for VAT on mandatory Form No. (1) VAT within 30 days of the date taxable turnover exceeds EGP 500,000, or earlier if voluntary registration is opted; ETA issues the VAT certificate under the same TIN coding. Step 4: Enroll in the ETA e-invoicing master data file and obtain API credentials/golden certificate before issuing any B2B/B2G invoice. Step 5: For export zero-rating, register the company in the ETA exporters register, open the export file, and provide the Egyptian bank account details for Central Bank of Egypt FX tracking.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (resident EG_LLC taxed on worldwide income at 22.5% CIT; non-resident sellers without PE taxed only on Egyptian-source income via withholding/deemed-profit rules; SCZone/Free-Zone licensed entities can elect exemption windows but pure SaaS helpdesk operations normally remain in the ordinary 22.5% regime)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election; ETA applies source rules and the general anti-avoidance rule (Art. 37 Income Tax Law 91/2005). Available statutory elections: (i) deemed-profit election under Art. 63 for non-resident service providers without PE (15% of gross as taxable profit); (ii) voluntary VAT registration below the EGP 500,000 threshold; (iii) cash-basis or invoice-basis VAT accounting election where bookkeeping standards permit; (iv) Free Zone/SCZone investment exemption election under Investment Law 72/2017 — not advantageous for B2B export services because the 0% VAT export regime already eliminates indirect tax leakage; (v) export incentive and penalty-relief election under the 2025 Tax Facilitation Package (Law 12/2025) preserving FX-based export benefits.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) under Law 67/2016 and Executive Regulation 66/2017; national stamp tax and customs duties are administered separately by ETA and Customs Authority.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies (VAT Art. 15). Foreign non-resident digital/e-services suppliers selling into Egypt without a local establishment must register for VAT irrespective of threshold under ETA Decree No. 633/2021; imports of the foreign parent SaaS platform into Egypt by EG_LLC trigger 14% reverse-charge VAT on the intercompany fees.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time B2B e-invoicing and B2C e-receipts phased in by ETA (large taxpayers 2021; all taxpayers in subsequent tranches through 2023-2024). Every invoice/receipt must be generated via ETA-approved systems, submitted within seconds to the ETA clearing platform (einvoicing.eta.gov.eg) through REST/API integration authenticated with the golden certificate, and bear an ETA-generated UUID, QR code and digital tracking stamp to be legally valid. Zero-rated export invoices must carry the Export transaction-type code, foreign customer TIN/country code, and the applicable FX rate per the ETA schema. Offline invoicing is prohibited; rejected invoices are legally void, force output VAT recovery, and block input VAT deduction.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies under VAT Law Art. 24/1 when the helpdesk/SaaS service is supplied by EG_LLC to a non-resident recipient, is consumed entirely outside Egypt (determined by customer location and benefit, not call-agent location), is paid in foreign currency, and is evidenced as an export in the ETA exporters register. Mixed-use or onshore assist elements such as serving Egyptian end-customers remain standard-rated at 14% and must be separately invoiced. Intercompany trials, dormant environments, or non-FX settlements will be recharacterized as taxable domestic supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Signed export service contract or master helpdesk subscription agreement with the non-resident customer
Commercial invoice and ETA-cleared e-invoice marked Export (0%) with ETA QR code and clearance UUID
ETA export register/export file registration confirmation for the service transaction
Bank credit advice or Foreign Currency Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) from an Egyptian authorized bank evidencing FX receipt
Central Bank of Egypt export proceeds repatriation confirmation (FX credited/surrendered to EG_LLC Egyptian bank account)
Service delivery and off-shore usage evidence: IP logs, non-resident customer contact details, usage analytics, and a certificate confirming non-Egyptian consumption
Goods-export annex (only when SaaS is embedded or ancillary to physical goods): customs export declaration and Bill of Lading/Airway Bill
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA cross-matches zero-rated invoices against bank FX inflows; if foreign-currency proceeds are not credited within the CBE window (typically 180 days for service exports), the 0% claim is retrospectively clawed back at 14% plus 2% monthly delay interest without goodwill. Fraudulent or false export claims trigger VAT evasion penalties (Art. 71-74, Law 67/2016): minimum fine EGP 20,000, maximum EGP 200,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years, forfeiture of input VAT credits, and joint personal liability of the tax representative and directors. E-invoice clearance misuse adds fines up to EGP 50,000 per invoice under Decree 501/2022 plus suspension of the exporter registration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), exercising exclusive jurisdiction under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020 and the accompanying foreign-exchange regulations, with delegated authority over authorized dealing banks, balance-of-payments reporting, capital-account administration, and all cross-border settlement currency approvals.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Following the 6 March 2024 exchange-rate unification and the adoption of a market-determined, durably flexible exchange-rate regime under the IMF Extended Fund Facility, the Egyptian pound (EGP) is freely tradable through CBE-licensed banks within a managed float. Current-account convertibility is substantially liberalized: cross-border payments for services, including SaaS subscriptions, cloud-hosting fees, intercompany service charges, and customer-support helpdesk software licenses, may be executed by authorized banks upon submission of the underlying commercial documents and a CBE balance-of-payments (BOP) purpose-code declaration. Capital-account convertibility remains administratively controlled: inbound equity injections require registration through an authorized bank under the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and General Authority for Investment (GAFI) procedures, whereas outbound profit remittances and capital repatriations require audited financial statements, an Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) clearance certificate, and proof that the foreign currency was lawfully acquired through the onshore banking system. Key practical hurdles include bank-level FX liquidity windows, enhanced purpose-code scrutiny on large invoices, and the need to maintain a clean, auditable FX origination trail.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE rules implementing Law No. 194 of 2020, all export proceeds from services and goods must be received into an Egyptian authorized bank and repatriated to Egypt within 90 days of the transaction effective date for services, extendable to 180 days with documented justification and bank approval. After the March 2024 liberalization, no mandatory conversion ratio applies: the prior emergency surrender requirement was suspended, and exporters may retain 100% of repatriated proceeds in onshore foreign-currency export or operational accounts or convert them at interbank rates. Compliance requires the LLC to: (i) submit software-export contracts and invoice cohorts to the receiving bank; (ii) tag each inbound digital-services receipt with the correct CBE BOP services code; (iii) route all proceeds exclusively to a CBE-licensed onshore account, because receipts held at offshore EMI or PSP accounts are not recognized as valid repatriation; and (iv) retain the complete CBE FX transaction file for at least five years for audit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with dedicated FX forward and margin revaluation sub-ledger
Operational Account (USD-denominated, non-resident director friendly, linked to parent treasury)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: MEDIUM for ancillary use only; LOW as a primary rail. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, or Currencycloud are not recognized by the CBE as banks or licensed payment-service providers and may not maintain EGP-denominated deposits or clear into the Egyptian interbank EGP system. They may operate solely as collection and aggregation gateways downstream of Stripe Billing and PayPal, provided the merchant agreements are in the LLC's name, funds are swept at least weekly via SWIFT MT103 to the CBE-licensed onshore operational account, and the EMI is not contractually designated as the CBE-recognized repatriation account. Any unlicensed foreign entity offering payment services to Egyptian residents would face CBE enforcement. Accordingly, the compliant architecture requires an onshore licensed bank as the sole liquidity hub; EMIs are permitted only as accelerant rails for aggregator receipts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is not fully available for first-time non-resident clients. Under CBE AML/CFT rules (Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended), each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and each authorized signatory must complete an identity verification interview; this generally requires the Egyptian resident manager or attorney-in-fact to appear physically at the branch while non-resident UBOs execute a notarized power of attorney before an Egyptian consulate or a notary subject to apostille or consular legalization. CIB and HSBC Egypt accept remote video onboarding for low-risk professional clients when corporate documents are apostilled and a live video compliance call is completed. NBE and Banque Misr ordinarily require physical attendance of at least one director or attorney-in-fact. Mandatory physical presence cannot be waived if any UBO is connected to a sanctioned or high-risk jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident 100% foreign ownership with no Egyptian tax identification number or demonstrable local economic nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled or consular-legalized certificate of incorporation and memorandum of the parent; notarized board resolution appointing the Egyptian manager or attorney-in-fact; certified CBE-format UBO declaration; certified passports of UBOs and signatories; executed Egyptian office lease or SCZone/private-free-zone arrangement; ETA tax-card application receipt; bank account mandate form.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency low-ticket inbound credits below USD 500 from Stripe or PayPal aggregators presenting a commingled deposit profile inconsistent with single-name invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed merchant service agreements with Stripe Billing and PayPal; monthly payout settlement reports and merchant earnings summaries; SaaS subscription catalog and plan structure reconciling ticket sizes; customer and subscription portfolio export; chargeback and refund policy documents; internal AML risk classification memo confirming a Low_Risk_Standard non-face-to-face profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid circuit movement or flicker: aggregator proceeds swept to an offshore EMI or shareholder account within 24 hours of credit, triggering structural transaction monitoring alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal treasury sweeping policy with a two-business-day holding period; liquidity forecast and FX ticket trail; underlying vendor agreements for outbound settlements with cloud or sub-processor and helpdesk subcontractors; bank-approved tiered transaction limits; monthly invoice-to-receipt-to-payment reconciliation report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Purpose-code or narrative mismatch on inbound MT103, such as stating software services but crediting capital, resulting in CBE unidentified-inflow classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Advance authorization letter from the bank's FX desk; completed CBE BOP purpose-code declaration; export invoices and order forms; SWIFT field-70 narrative standardized to match the declared purpose code; lawyer's opinion characterizing the transaction; standing instruction with the bank for code harmonization.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound dividend, royalty, or service remittances to non-resident shareholders before fulfillment of the CBE 180-day export-proceeds holding period or ETA tax-clearance requirements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements for the relevant period; ETA tax clearance certificate and withholding tax evidence under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 or applicable treaty relief; CBE approval or authorized-bank confirmation for repatriation; audited FX ledger evidencing that retained proceeds originated from registered export receipts; board dividend resolution with distribution timing memorandum.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder shall subscribe equity via SWIFT MT103 to the LLC's onshore foreign-currency account at an authorized bank. The payment order must include the correct CBE BOP purpose code for inward direct investment in equity, a narrative field stating 'Capital subscription to [LLC name], Commercial Register [number], Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 registration [IFD number]', and a reference to the capital-increase board resolution to preempt unidentified-inflow flags. The bank will verify the investor's GAFI-filed incorporation file, apostilled board resolutions, the UBO/shareholding list, and the LLC's commercial-register capacity to receive the amount; no minimum capital requirement blocks the subscription. Shareholder loans must be routed under the CBE intercompany-lending purpose code with a signed term sheet to prevent recharacterization as equity or deemed distribution. For any future exit or dividend repatriation, the LLC must present audited financials, ETA clearance, and the bank-issued evidence of registration of the initial inflow to activate the CBE repatriation allowance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SaaS and trade disbursements are settled via SWIFT MT103 for single outbound payments, or, where bank-requested security applies, through a commercial letter of credit issued by the authorized bank; LCs are primarily relevant to goods rather than digital services. Each outbound MT103 must carry the correct CBE outbound services purpose code, such as computer and data-processing services, royalties, license fees, or import of services, and be supported by the underlying contract or order, the supplier invoice, and non-resident beneficiary withholding documentation where applicable under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 or an applicable double-tax treaty. Banks will not release FX above their internal invoice-clearing threshold without ETA remittance clearance. For recurring payouts to global cloud and helpdesk sub-processors, the LLC should implement an approved aggregate-invoice sweep arrangement, processing weekly or monthly batch MT103s against one statement of work, to minimize redundant KYC on each debit. The onshore FX account should maintain a minimum 45-day disbursement runway to avoid forced conversions in illiquid interbank windows. Stripe Billing and PayPal settlement currencies should be automatically swept to the onshore USD account on a daily notional basis.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore USD/EGP FX forward contracts with CBE-authorized banks, tenors typically up to 180 days, backed by documented commercial or trade exposure, with margin deposits of 10% to 15%.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on EGP executed by the parent treasury outside Egypt, permitted for risk management of the EGP-denominated cost base of the USD-functional LLC, with post-trade reporting through the local authorized bank.
Cross-currency USD/EGP swaps, including spot-for-forward and forward-forward structures, with the onshore relationship bank for liquidity conversion timing and reinvestment yield management.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps under ISDA with offshore counterparties for balance-sheet hedging of intercompany loans, subject to CBE no-objection and documented underlying exposure.
Vanilla OTC USD/EGP options, which are not permitted onshore unless trade-backed and pre-approved by the CBE; available only offshore under a strict parent-hedging mandate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return with audited financial statements and tax reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers monthly statutory delinquency charges on unpaid tax, rejection of unaudited deductions, enforced collection via bank attachment, and possible administrative strike-off after sustained non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Foreign Trade (GAFI) — Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based; the renewal application must be completed before the current certificate expires, normally within 30 days after the anniversary of original registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An expired commercial registration invalidates bank mandates, notarization, contracts and import authorizations; late renewal attracts GAFI late fees and a lapse exceeding one year may trigger administrative deletion from the Commercial Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation statement and UBO register update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Commercial Registry — UBO filing window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any shareholding transfer or UBO change; a confirmation statement must also be attached to the annual Commercial Registration renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to disclose UBO changes within 30 days gives rise to fines under Egypt's anti-money laundering law and Commercial Registry regulations; persistent inaccuracy may lead to criminal liability, invalidation of the register and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Periodic value-added tax returns and annual VAT reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly VAT declarations are due by the last business day of the month following the tax period; the final period return in the fiscal year operates as the annual VAT reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late VAT filing produces automatic daily fines per period and late-payment interest; continued delinquency results in ETA summary assessments, asset attachment and suspension of cooperation certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual social insurance wage declaration and payroll reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Social Insurance Authority of Egypt
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual wage statement filed during the first quarter after the calendar year-end; monthly contribution statements remain due throughout the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or false wage declarations give rise to contribution surcharges, social insurance inspections, personal liability of managers and administrative restriction of import/export privileges.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian LLCs must appoint at least one licensed auditor under Companies Law No. 159/1981; the ETA additionally requires audited accounts for taxpayers with gross revenue exceeding EGP 10 million or total assets exceeding EGP 20 million. Dormant LLCs may obtain ETA consent to file a nil return without certified accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) — largely converged with IFRS; consolidated financial statements of groups filing in Egypt apply IFRS as endorsed and supervised by the Egyptian Ministry of Finance and Financial Regulatory Authority.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Any shareholding transfer or change in the natural-person beneficial ownership chain of 25% or more must be recorded in the statutory UBO register within 30 days. At the annual Commercial Registry renewal, the LLC manager must confirm under penalty of perjury that the beneficial ownership register is current and attach the updated UBO disclosure when required by GAFI; the annual confirmation is bundled into the standard renewal package where this applies.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders and share-transfer history)
Register of Directors (and managers for LLC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350–1,200 per year for registered-office service in Cairo/Giza; USD 200–700 for a single-purpose mail-forwarding address in other governorates.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,000–2,800 for a low-risk customer-support helpdesk LLC with standard cloud subscription revenue; USD 3,000–6,500 if the audit scope includes intercompany transactions, payroll registrations, VAT refund claims or multi-entity consolidation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% (Law No. 91 of 2005 as amended by Law No. 26 of 2020, applicable to tax periods commencing on or after 1 January 2020)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket statutory income tax holiday for ISIC 6201 helpdesk/SaaS activities. Available reliefs: (i) Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise Law No. 152 of 2020 allows an elective final turnover tax of approximately 0.5%-1% on annual gross receipts for qualifying small helpdesk companies within stipulated revenue ceilings; (ii) Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 provides investment-cost allowances, employment-linked deductions and spatial incentives for projects in the Suez Canal Economic Zone and licensed technology parks; (iii) export-proceeds banked in Egypt may qualify for enhanced cost deductions on foreign-source service revenue; (iv) foreign tax credits under double-taxation agreements. Absent a valid election or zone incentive, the effective base rate for the LLC remains 22.5%.
